rules.statement: Implement a single-use or replay check with an atomic add-if-absent operation on the shared store, never as a read followed by a write (for example `IDistributedCache.GetAsync` then `SetAsync`).
rules.why: A read-then-write lets two concurrent presentations of the same proof or assertion both be accepted, on one replica or on two that share a store.
rules.check: Look for replay, nonce or single-use checks that call a get/contains method and then a set/add method separately, or that are built on `IDistributedCache`.

rules.statement: Redeem a one-time record (such as a login transaction) with an atomic take that removes and returns the entry in one step, not with a get followed by a remove.
rules.why: With an atomic take, a replayed callback finds nothing. A separate get and remove lets two concurrent callbacks both redeem it.
rules.check: Look for code that reads a one-time entry and then deletes it in separate calls instead of using a take/GETDEL-style operation.

rules.statement: Update shared state that concurrent requests may modify with a versioned compare-and-swap, not with an unconditional overwrite.
rules.why: Without compare-and-swap, two concurrent requests that refresh the same record overwrite each other.
rules.check: Look for shared session or state updates that write the new value with a plain set and don't check the version read earlier.

rules.statement: In library code, don't register host-wide infrastructure services such as `IDistributedCache`. Depend on the library's own ports and let the composition root choose the adapter.
rules.why: Registering such a service from a library decides it for the host and for every other consumer of it.
rules.check: Look for `AddDistributedMemoryCache`, `AddStackExchangeRedisCache` or other registrations of shared framework services inside a library's service-collection extensions.

rules.statement: Build shared-store keys from request-supplied values as a purpose prefix, the tenant and a digest (such as the base64url SHA-256 of the length-prefixed UTF-8 components), never by joining raw values with a separator.
rules.why: Values joined with `:` are ambiguous (`("a:b","c")` and `("a","b:c")` give the same key) and unbounded in length, and a key that names no tenant collides across the tenants that share the store.
rules.check: Look for store keys made with string interpolation or concatenation of request values, or keys that leave out the tenant.

rules.statement: When a security check relies on a shared store, make it fail closed: an expiry that isn't in the future records nothing and the add fails, and an unreachable store throws instead of being treated as a missing or new entry.
rules.why: Treating a failed or degenerate store operation as success would let replays through or treat a session that can't be read as absent.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks around store calls that return success, null or 'absent', and for adds that accept a past or current expiry.

rules.statement: An in-process store that keeps caller-supplied byte buffers must copy them on write instead of keeping the caller's memory.
rules.why: Otherwise a caller that reuses its buffer can change an entry that is already stored.
rules.check: Look for store implementations that save a `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>` or array argument directly without copying it.

rules.statement: Configuration and startup validation errors must never include a connection string or any of its parts.
rules.why: Connection strings and their parts may hold a password.
rules.check: Look for exception messages or log calls that interpolate connection strings, host/user/password parts or raw configuration values.

rules.statement: Values written to a shared external store are opaque bytes that the caller serializes, and the caller encrypts any value that must not be readable in the store.
rules.why: The store is outside the process and can be read by whoever operates it, so it must not hold secrets in clear.
rules.check: Look for tokens or other sensitive session data written to a shared store without encryption.

rules.statement: Compute expiry times-to-live for a shared store from the local `TimeProvider` clock and round them up to whole milliseconds, so expiry doesn't depend on the server's clock.
rules.why: Expiry then follows the replica's own clock, and rounding up keeps a record from expiring before it should.
rules.check: Look for TTL calculations that truncate or round down to milliseconds, or that rely on server-side time.

rules.statement: Put an adapter that brings a heavy third-party client (such as a Redis client) in a separate opt-in package, not in the core or turnkey package.
rules.why: Otherwise every consumer, including single-instance self-hosters, carries a client it doesn't use.
rules.check: Look for new package references to backend clients such as StackExchange.Redis added to core library projects.
